You are building chunk C3 of cpanel-mail-mcp, a Cloudflare Worker remote MCP server that gives Claude IMAP access to Scott's three cPanel business mailboxes. Read `docs/spec.md` (tag `spec-v1.1`), `docs/build/traceability.md`, `docs/prerequisites.md` and `docs/build/spec-questions.md` before writing code.

## Goal

Build header decoding and encoding, MIME parsing and building, CommonMark rendering, quoting, threading headers and signatures, as pure functions.

## Rules for this chunk (read first)

1. Build to `docs/spec.md` at git tag `spec-v1.1`. Do not edit `docs/spec.md`, `docs/rule-base.md`, `docs/ambiguity-log.md` or `docs/design.md`.
2. Implement only the requirements listed under "In scope". Do not add behavior the spec does not state, even if it seems obviously useful.
3. If a requirement is unclear, contradicts another, or needs a decision the spec does not make: do not decide it. Add an entry to `docs/build/spec-questions.md` (format below), skip that item, finish the rest, and list the question in the PR. Scott resolves it and, if needed, the spec gets a version bump.
4. Every automated test's name starts with the REQ IDs it verifies, for example `REQ-4-7 REQ-4-8: greeting times out after 5 s`.
5. Fill the "Verified by" column of `docs/build/traceability.md` for every in-scope row (test file and test name, or the manual check to perform). Set Status to `built` for automated rows that pass, or `needs Scott` for manual rows.
6. No secrets in the repo, logs, test output or PR. Passwords are entered by Scott with `wrangler secret put` only. Never print a secret value.
7. Work on branch `chunk/C3`. Open a pull request titled `C3: Headers, MIME, signatures`. Do not merge it. Stop after opening the PR.
8. The PR description contains: in-scope REQs and their status, the exact commands you ran with their pass/fail results, anything deferred and why, and any spec questions raised.

|---|---|---|
| REQ-10-1 | automated test | The server appends the account's configured signature to every draft it creates or edits (decision D1); skills keep sending signature-free bodies. |
| REQ-10-2 | automated test | The server, not Spark, appends the signature; Spark does not sign drafts it did not create. |
| REQ-10-3 | automated test | Signature texts are exactly: scott@reasinger.net = "Scott Reasinger / scott@reasinger.net / 317-460-0736 / https://linkedin.com/in/scottreasinger"; scott@yourcigardeni... |

| REQ-10-7 | automated test | An edit with no new body re-derives the body from the stored draft minus its signature before re-signing. |
| REQ-10-8 | automated test | In replies and forwards the signature goes directly under Scott's new text, above the quoted original. |
| REQ-10-9 | automated test | The signature bypasses markdown rendering. In the text part it is the exact configured string. In the HTML part it is the same string HTML-escaped in its own block, wi... |
| REQ-10-10 | automated test | "The draft body carries no signature" refers to the body the skill sends to the server, not the stored draft; the stored draft carries the server signature. |
| REQ-10-11 | automated test | No configured signature may contain sreasinger@gmail.com. |
| REQ-11-1 | automated test | The server decodes all returned header text (subjects and address display names arrive RFC 2047 encoded) before returning it. |
| REQ-11-2 | automated test | The server builds `Re:` and `Fwd:` subjects from the decoded subject. |
| REQ-11-3 | automated test | On write, the server re-encodes a non-ASCII subject; this is a tested gate. |

| REQ-14-9 | automated test | Test: resubmitting a signed body yields exactly one signature. |
| REQ-14-10 | automated test | Unit test: the scott@reasinger.net signature config string equals the gatekeeper check-file signature line. |
| REQ-14-11 | automated test | Config test: fails if any configured signature contains sreasinger@gmail.com. |
| REQ-14-15 | automated test | Test: a re-encoded non-ASCII subject on write. |
| REQ-18-8 | automated test | Draft bodies are parsed as CommonMark. Quoted originals in replies and forwards follow the format Spark produces. |

## Deliverables

- RFC 2047 decode for all returned header text; re-encode non-ASCII subjects on write; Re: and Fwd: from decoded subjects (section 11).
- MIME parsing for snippets and plain-text thread bodies.
- MIME builder: multipart text and HTML from CommonMark, quote format matching Spark, In-Reply-To and References (REQ-18-8, REQ-11-4).
- Signatures: exact texts from REQ-10-3, strip-then-append once, placement above quoted original, bypass markdown, HTML rendering rule (section 10).

## Required tests

- Signature resubmit yields one signature (REQ-14-9).
- scott@reasinger.net signature string equals the gatekeeper check-file line (REQ-14-10).
- Config test fails on any signature containing sreasinger@gmail.com (REQ-14-11).
- Non-ASCII subject re-encode (REQ-14-15). Decode tests using the real encoded subjects in the C1 fixtures.
